questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text:
زار وفد من طلاب جامعة إبادان معرض الكتاب الدولي في القاهرة الشهر الماضي. شاهد الطلاب آلاف الكتب في مختلف المجالات، من الأدب والتاريخ إلى العلوم الحديثة. التقى الوفد بعدد من الكتّاب المصريين وتحدثوا معهم عن أهمية القراءة في بناء المجتمع. في نهاية الزيارة، اشترى كل طالب عدداً من الكتب العربية ليأخذها معه إلى نيجيريا، وعبّروا عن أملهم في تكرار هذه الزيارة كل عام.

options: إلى معرض الكتاب الدولي في القاهرة
questions.explanation: The passage states 'زار وفد من طلاب جامعة إبادان معرض الكتاب الدولي في القاهرة' (a delegation visited the International Book Fair in Cairo).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text:
تشتهر مدينة كانو في شمال نيجيريا بأسواقها القديمة وتاريخها الإسلامي العريق. يقصد كثير من طلاب العلم هذه المدينة لدراسة اللغة العربية والعلوم الإسلامية في مدارسها التقليدية. ومن أشهر هذه المدارس ما يُعرف بنظام 'التعليم العتيق'، الذي يعتمد على حفظ القرآن الكريم وتعلم النحو والفقه على يد شيوخ متخصصين. يرى كثير من الباحثين أن هذا النظام التعليمي حافظ على اللغة العربية حية بين المسلمين في غرب أفريقيا لقرون طويلة.

ما معنى كلمة 'العريق' كما وردت في وصف تاريخ كانو؟
questions.explanation: 'العريق' means 'deep-rooted/ancient and authentic', describing a long-established and distinguished history.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to Arabic: 'The teacher explains the lesson clearly.'
questions.explanation: 'The teacher explains the lesson clearly' becomes 'المعلم يشرح الدرس بوضوح', using يشرح (explains) and بوضوح (clearly).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to Arabic: 'The students visited the university library.'
questions.explanation: 'The students visited the university library' is 'زار الطلاب مكتبة الجامعة', using the past-tense verb زار (visited) with مكتبة الجامعة (the university library).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to Arabic: 'My father works as a doctor in the hospital.'
questions.explanation: 'My father works as a doctor in the hospital' translates as 'يعمل أبي طبيباً في المستشفى', with أبي (my father), طبيباً (as a doctor, accusative), and المستشفى (the hospital).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to Arabic: 'These students are diligent in their studies.'
questions.explanation: 'These students are diligent in their studies' is 'هؤلاء الطلاب مجتهدون في دراستهم', using the plural demonstrative هؤلاء and the sound masculine plural مجتهدون.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to Arabic: 'The new library will open next month.'
questions.explanation: 'The new library will open next month' uses the future marker سـ with تفتح, giving 'ستفتح المكتبة الجديدة الشهر القادم'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to English: 'زارت الأسرة جدها في القرية.'
options: The family built a new house
The family visited their grandfather in the village
The children played in the garden
questions.explanation: 'زارت الأسرة جدها في القرية' translates as 'The family visited their grandfather in the village', using زارت (visited, feminine agreeing with الأسرة).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to English: 'يجب على الطالب أن يذاكر دروسه جيداً.'
options: The teacher must correct the exams
The student refuses to attend school
The student must study his lessons well
The student forgot his books at home
questions.explanation: 'يجب على الطالب أن يذاكر دروسه جيداً' means 'The student must study his lessons well', using يجب على (it is necessary upon) with the subjunctive verb يذاكر.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to English: 'كتبت الطالبة رسالة إلى صديقتها.'
options: The boy drew a picture of his school
The teacher read a newspaper article
The mother cooked dinner for the family
The (female) student wrote a letter to her friend
questions.explanation: 'كتبت الطالبة رسالة إلى صديقتها' translates as 'The (female) student wrote a letter to her friend', with كتبت (wrote, feminine) and رسالة (a letter).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to English: 'سافر التجار إلى المدينة لبيع بضائعهم.'
options: The farmers stayed home to harvest their crops
The merchants travelled to the city to sell their goods
The students travelled abroad to study medicine
The soldiers returned to their camp at night
questions.explanation: 'سافر التجار إلى المدينة لبيع بضائعهم' translates as 'The merchants travelled to the city to sell their goods', using لبيع (to sell) to express purpose.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Turn to English: 'لا تتأخر عن موعد الامتحان غداً.'
options: Do not forget your book at home today
Do not speak loudly in the library
Do not be late for the exam appointment tomorrow
Do not travel without your parents' permission
questions.explanation: 'لا تتأخر عن موعد الامتحان غداً' is a negative command meaning 'Do not be late for the exam appointment tomorrow', using لا with the jussive تتأخر.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following best defines a verb (فعل) in Arabic grammar?
options: A word that names a person, place or thing only
A word that expresses an action or event linked to a particular time
A particle that has no independent meaning of its own
A word used exclusively to introduce questions
questions.explanation: A verb (فعل) in Arabic denotes an action or occurrence tied to a specific tense (past, present, or imperative), distinguishing it from nouns (اسم) and particles (حرف).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: A particle (حرف) in Arabic grammar is best described as a word that
options: has no independent meaning by itself and only gains meaning in relation to other words
forms the subject of every sentence
is always conjugated for tense like a verb
questions.explanation: Particles (حروف), such as prepositions and conjunctions, do not carry independent meaning on their own but instead connect or modify other words in a sentence.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct sound masculine plural of the word مُهَنْدِس (engineer)?
questions.explanation: The sound masculine plural is formed by adding ون to the singular, giving مُهَنْدِسُون (engineers, masculine).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct sound feminine plural of the word طَالِبَة (female student)?
questions.explanation: The sound feminine plural adds ات to the singular, giving طَالِبَات (female students).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following words is an example of a broken plural (جمع تكسير)?
questions.explanation: رِجَال is a broken plural formed by an internal pattern change from the singular رَجُل, unlike the regular sound plurals in the other options.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The dual form (المثنى) of the noun كِتَاب (book) in the nominative case is
questions.explanation: The dual in the nominative case is formed by adding ان to the singular noun, giving كِتَابَان (two books); كِتَابَيْن is the accusative/genitive form.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following is a detached (separable) subject pronoun in Arabic?
questions.explanation: هِيَ (she) is a detached pronoun that stands independently as a subject, unlike the other options, which are attached (suffixed) pronouns.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In the phrase 'بيتُهُ' (his house), the attached pronoun ـهُ indicates
options: possession, showing the house belongs to him
questions.explanation: The suffixed pronoun ـهُ attached to a noun expresses possession, so بيتُهُ literally means 'his house'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The demonstrative pronoun ذلك is generally used in Arabic to mean
options: this (masculine singular, referring to something near)
that (masculine singular, referring to something farther away)
questions.explanation: ذلك specifically indicates 'that' for a masculine singular noun that is relatively distant, as opposed to هذا which indicates 'this' for something nearby.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The relative pronoun التي in Arabic is used specifically to refer back to a preceding noun that is
questions.explanation: التي (allati) is the relative pronoun used when the antecedent is a feminine singular noun, corresponding to الذي for masculine singular nouns.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: A verb such as أعطى (to give), which requires two objects to complete its meaning, is classified as
options: a doubly transitive verb (فعل متعدٍ إلى مفعولين)
questions.explanation: Verbs like أعطى (to give) that require two objects — for example, 'he gave the student a book' — are classified as doubly transitive verbs.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The past tense verb ذَهَبَ (he went) belongs to which category of Arabic verb tense?
questions.explanation: ذَهَبَ is conjugated in the past (perfect) tense, indicating a completed action.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following is the correct imperative (فعل الأمر) form derived from the verb كَتَبَ (he wrote)?
questions.explanation: The imperative form اُكْتُبْ (write!) is derived from the root ك-ت-ب, used to issue a direct command.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The particle لن is used in Arabic grammar specifically to negate
options: a future action, requiring the following verb to be in the subjunctive mood
a present habitual action, with no mood change
questions.explanation: لن (lan) is a particle of negation used specifically for the future, and it places the following imperfect verb in the subjunctive mood, e.g. لن أذهب (I will not go).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The particle لَمَّا, when used before a past-tense-meaning imperfect verb, generally functions to mean
options: 'not yet' or 'when' depending on context, negating up to the present or marking a past temporal clause
questions.explanation: لَمَّا has two common uses: as a negation meaning 'not yet' (with a jussive verb) or as a temporal conjunction meaning 'when' introducing a past-time clause.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In the sentence 'كانَ الجوُّ بارداً', the word بارداً is in the accusative case because
options: it is a broken plural noun
it is the predicate (خبر) of كان, which كان places in the accusative
it is the subject of the sentence
questions.explanation: كان and its sister verbs keep the subject (اسم كان) in the nominative but shift the predicate (خبر كان) into the accusative case, as with بارداً here.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In the sentence 'إنّ الطقسَ جميلٌ', the word الطقسَ is in the accusative case because
options: it is the subject (اسم إنّ) of إنّ, which places its subject in the accusative
it is the predicate of the sentence
questions.explanation: إنّ and its sister particles place the subject that follows them (اسم إنّ) in the accusative case, while the predicate (خبر إنّ) remains nominative.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which case is used for the noun immediately following a preposition such as فِي (in) or عَلَى (on)?
options: No case marking applies after prepositions
questions.explanation: Any noun following a preposition (حرف جر) is placed in the genitive case, a defining rule of Arabic case grammar.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: When counting nouns using the numbers 11 to 99 (excluding multiples of 10), the counted noun generally appears in which form?
options: Singular, and in the accusative case
Plural, and in the nominative case only
Plural, and in the genitive case
questions.explanation: Unlike numbers 3-10, numbers from 11 to 99 (excluding exact tens) typically require the counted noun to be singular and in the accusative case, e.g. 'عشرون طالباً' (twenty students).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The idafa construction (الإضافة), such as in 'مكتبة الجامعة' (the university's library), links two nouns where the second noun (المضاف إليه) is placed in which case?
questions.explanation: In an idafa construction, the second noun (المضاف إليه) that indicates possession or association is always placed in the genitive case.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following correctly illustrates subject-verb gender agreement when the verb precedes a feminine subject?
questions.explanation: Since the subject الطالبة (the female student) is feminine, the verb must carry the feminine marker تْ, giving ذَهَبَتْ.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The negative particle ليس is grammatically significant in Arabic because it
options: functions like كان and its sisters, placing its predicate in the accusative case while negating a nominal sentence
is used only to negate verbs in the past tense
questions.explanation: ليس (laysa) behaves grammatically like كان, negating a nominal sentence in the present while placing its predicate (خبر ليس) in the accusative case.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a comparative/superlative adjective pattern (اسم التفضيل) in Arabic?
questions.explanation: أَكْبَر follows the أفعل pattern typical of comparative and superlative adjectives in Arabic, derived from the root ك-ب-ر (big).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following best represents the correct structure of a simple Arabic nominal sentence (subject + predicate)?
options: أن الجوَّ حارٌّ (with a subordinating particle only)
حارٌّ الجوُّ (with reversed word order only in poetry)
يكونُ الجوُّ حارٌّ دائماً (with an extra auxiliary needed)
questions.explanation: A basic nominal sentence in Arabic simply pairs a topic (مبتدأ) with its predicate (خبر), as in الجوُّ حارٌّ, without needing any linking verb such as 'to be'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Arabic numerals differ from English numerals in that, within Arabic-Indic numeral notation used in many Arabic texts, numbers are generally written and read
options: in reverse order compared to spoken numerals
from left to right, unlike the surrounding Arabic script which reads right to left
from right to left, exactly like the surrounding Arabic script
top to bottom, unlike any other language
questions.explanation: Even though Arabic script is written right to left, multi-digit numerals (whether Arabic-Indic or Western Arabic numerals) are conventionally written and read left to right.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The word عِلْم (knowledge) is grammatically classified as
options: a verb expressing a past action
a feminine noun (اسم مؤنث) due to a ta marbuta ending
questions.explanation: عِلْم has no feminine marker such as ta marbuta and is treated as a masculine noun in Arabic grammar.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The verb noun (المصدر) derived from the verb دَرَسَ (he studied) is
questions.explanation: دِرَاسَة is the verbal noun (مصدر) of دَرَسَ, expressing the abstract concept or act of 'studying'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The active participle (اسم الفاعل) derived from the verb كَتَبَ (he wrote) is
questions.explanation: كَاتِب is the active participle (اسم الفاعل) of كَتَبَ, referring to the one performing the action of writing.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The passive participle (اسم المفعول) derived from the verb فَهِمَ (he understood) is
questions.explanation: مَفْهُوم is the passive participle (اسم المفعول) of فَهِمَ, describing something that has been understood.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which particle among the following introduces a subordinate clause meaning 'because' in Arabic?
questions.explanation: لأنّ (li'anna) is a causal particle used to introduce a clause explaining the reason for something, equivalent to 'because' in English.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In writing a formal Arabic application letter (طلب), which opening phrase is most appropriate?
options: أتقدم بطلبي هذا راجياً النظر فيه
questions.explanation: 'أتقدم بطلبي هذا راجياً النظر فيه' (I submit this application hoping it will be considered) is a standard formal opening for a written application in Arabic.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: When composing a paragraph describing a past journey in Arabic, the writer should primarily use
options: only nominal sentences with no verbs
the perfect (past) tense to narrate completed events
questions.explanation: Since the events being described already occurred, the past (perfect) tense is the appropriate choice for narrating a completed journey.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following connecting words would best link two contrasting ideas in an Arabic composition?
questions.explanation: لكنّ is a contrastive conjunction used to connect two ideas that oppose or differ from one another, similar to 'but' in English.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following expressions is appropriate for expressing an apology in Arabic composition?
questions.explanation: 'أعتذر عن التأخير' (I apologise for the delay) is a standard phrase for expressing an apology, suitable for both formal and semi-formal writing.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In composing a paragraph giving instructions or directions, which verb form is most naturally used?
questions.explanation: Instructions and directions are naturally conveyed using direct commands, making the imperative mood (فعل الأمر) the most suitable verb form.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which sequencing word would best help order steps in an Arabic composition describing a process?
options: هل... هل... هل (is it... is it... is it)
questions.explanation: Sequencing markers like أولاً (firstly), ثم (then), and أخيراً (finally) help organise steps clearly in a process description.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following would be an appropriate way to begin a persuasive composition arguing for a position?
options: لا أعرف شيئاً عن هذا الموضوع
questions.explanation: 'أرى أنّ من الضروري أن...' (I believe it is necessary that...) is a clear, assertive opening suited to a persuasive piece of writing.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: When writing a short biography (سيرة ذاتية) in Arabic, which tense predominantly describes the subject's life events?
questions.explanation: Biographical writing chronicles events that have already happened in a person's life, so the past tense is the natural primary tense used.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of the following best demonstrates a well-formed topic sentence opening a descriptive paragraph about a city?
options: لا شيء يستحق الذكر عن هذه المدينة
تُعدّ مدينة إبادان من أكبر المدن في نيجيريا
questions.explanation: A strong topic sentence introduces the main subject clearly and sets up the paragraph's focus, as this sentence does by identifying Ibadan as one of Nigeria's largest cities.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In Arabic composition, the correct use of gender agreement between an adjective and a feminine noun is shown in which example?
questions.explanation: Since مدينة (city) is feminine, its adjective must also take the feminine form جميلة, demonstrating correct gender agreement.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which closing expression is most suitable for an email to a university lecturer requesting an extension?
questions.explanation: This formal closing (please accept my sincere thanks and appreciation) suits respectful academic correspondence, unlike the casual alternatives.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: When composing a paragraph comparing two things in Arabic, which structure word is most useful?
questions.explanation: بينما (whereas) is a comparative/contrastive connector well suited to drawing distinctions between two items in a composition.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Imru' al-Qays, one of the most celebrated poets of the Pre-Islamic (Jahili) era, is particularly renowned for
options: founding a school of Islamic jurisprudence
his Mu'allaqa, considered one of the greatest odes of classical Arabic poetry
questions.explanation: Imru' al-Qays is widely regarded as one of the foremost Pre-Islamic poets, and his ode is traditionally counted among the celebrated Mu'allaqat.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The Jahiliyyah (Pre-Islamic) period is significant in Arabic literary history mainly because it
options: marked the beginning of printed Arabic books
was the first period in which Arabic prose novels appeared
produced a rich tradition of oral poetry that set early standards for classical Arabic verse
was dominated entirely by translated Greek texts
questions.explanation: The Jahiliyyah era is remembered chiefly for its highly developed oral poetic tradition, which established many of the stylistic conventions later classical Arabic poetry followed.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The Mu'allaqat are traditionally understood to be a collection of
options: collections of Hadith compiled in the Abbasid era
letters written by early Islamic caliphs
outstanding Pre-Islamic odes attributed to a small group of celebrated poets
questions.explanation: The Mu'allaqat refers to a set of especially esteemed odes by a handful of Pre-Islamic poets, traditionally regarded as pinnacles of pre-Islamic poetic achievement.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Hassan bin Thabit, a poet of the early Islamic period, is particularly known as
options: a compiler of pre-Islamic proverbs only
a poet closely associated with Prophet Muhammad, often called a defender of Islam through poetry
questions.explanation: Hassan bin Thabit was a companion of the Prophet Muhammad known for composing poetry in defence of Islam, earning him a distinguished place in early Islamic literary history.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Al-Farazdaq, an Umayyad-era poet, is chiefly remembered in Arabic literary history for
options: his poetic rivalry (naqa'id) with the poet Jarir
questions.explanation: Al-Farazdaq is best known for his long and celebrated poetic feud with Jarir, a defining feature of Umayyad-era satirical poetry (naqa'id).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The Abbasid period is often regarded as a golden age of Arabic literature primarily because of
options: the exclusive focus on oral tradition, with no written works
the total absence of poetry during this era
its complete isolation from other cultures and languages
the flourishing of scholarship, translation, poetry and prose, especially centred in Baghdad
questions.explanation: The Abbasid era saw an extraordinary flourishing of intellectual and literary activity, with Baghdad becoming a major hub for scholarship, translation and literary production.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Al-Mutanabbi, a celebrated Abbasid-era poet, is particularly noted for
options: compiling the Qur'an into its final written form
his role as a Rightly Guided Caliph
his eloquent and highly regarded classical Arabic poetry, still widely studied today
questions.explanation: Al-Mutanabbi is one of the most celebrated poets in the Arabic literary canon, renowned for his eloquence, and his poetry remains widely studied in the modern era.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The Nahda, a term significant to modern Arabic literary history, generally refers to
options: the fall of the Abbasid Caliphate
a specific style of West African Islamic scholarship
a period of Arab cultural and literary revival beginning around the 19th century
questions.explanation: The Nahda refers to the Arab literary and cultural renaissance that began roughly in the 19th century, marked by renewed engagement with classical heritage and modern influences.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Taha Hussein, a major figure of modern Arabic literature, is particularly recognised as
options: a prominent Egyptian writer and intellectual, notable for his influential autobiography and literary criticism
one of the Rightly Guided Caliphs
a compiler of early Hadith collections
questions.explanation: Taha Hussein was a leading figure of modern Egyptian and Arabic literature, well known for his influential works of autobiography and literary criticism.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Naguib Mahfouz, a significant name in modern Arabic literature, is particularly known for
options: his position as an early Islamic caliph
his novels depicting Egyptian society, for which he received international literary recognition
his role as a Pre-Islamic poet
his career exclusively as a poet with no prose works
questions.explanation: Naguib Mahfouz is widely celebrated for his novels portraying Egyptian society and received the Nobel Prize in Literature, a landmark achievement for modern Arabic fiction.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Sheikh Uthman Dan Fodio, a key figure associated with West African Arabic literary and scholarly tradition, is chiefly remembered for
options: his role as a Pre-Islamic Arabian poet
leading the Sokoto Jihad and producing significant Arabic-language Islamic scholarly works
questions.explanation: Uthman Dan Fodio led the Sokoto Jihad in what is now Northern Nigeria and authored numerous Arabic-language works on Islamic scholarship, making him central to West African Arabic literary history.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: West African Arabic scholarly literature associated with the Sokoto Caliphate is significant chiefly because it
options: was written exclusively in the Hausa language
demonstrates the deep historical roots of Arabic and Islamic scholarship in the West African region
shows a complete absence of Arabic influence in West Africa
questions.explanation: The scholarly output of the Sokoto Caliphate era illustrates the long-standing and significant presence of Arabic language and Islamic learning in West Africa, predating colonial contact.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The qasida (قصيدة), a major poetic form in classical Arabic literature, is best described as
options: a short modern free-verse poem with no fixed structure
a structured, often lengthy ode following classical rules of metre and rhyme
a form of prose fiction with no poetic elements
a type of formal legal document
questions.explanation: The qasida is the classical form of the Arabic ode, traditionally composed with a consistent metre and a single rhyme scheme running through the poem.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The term 'su'luk' (vagabond poets), associated with figures like Al-Shanfara and Ta'abbata Sharran, refers to poets who were characterised by
options: living outside normal tribal structures and composing poetry of individualism and hardship
serving as official court poets to caliphs
questions.explanation: The su'luk poets were often outcasts from their tribes, and their poetry frequently reflects themes of solitary struggle, independence, and survival outside conventional tribal life.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The historical progression of Arabic literature is typically studied across which broad chronological periods?
options: Only the Abbasid period, in isolation from all other eras
Only the period before the revelation of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Arabic literary history is conventionally organised into the Pre-Islamic era, the early Islamic through Umayyad and Abbasid classical era, and the Modern period.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The revelation of the Qur'an is considered a major turning point in Arabic literary history chiefly because it
options: was written in a non-Arabic language originally
ended all forms of poetry in Arabic permanently
had no influence on the Arabic language at all
established a new standard of linguistic eloquence that profoundly shaped later Arabic prose and poetry
questions.explanation: The Qur'an set an unprecedented standard of linguistic and rhetorical excellence in Arabic, which subsequently influenced the development of classical Arabic prose and poetry.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Ghazal (غزل), a recognised genre within classical and later Arabic poetry, primarily deals with themes of
questions.explanation: Ghazal is the traditional Arabic poetic genre centred on themes of love, beauty, and romantic longing, distinct from other poetic genres like elegy or satire.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Rithaa' (رثاء), a recognised genre of classical Arabic poetry, is primarily concerned with
options: elegy and mourning for the deceased
questions.explanation: Rithaa' is the elegiac genre of Arabic poetry, composed to mourn and commemorate someone who has died.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Hija' (هجاء), a recognised genre of classical Arabic poetry, particularly associated with poets like Jarir and Al-Farazdaq, is best described as
options: poetry praising a patron or ruler
satirical poetry aimed at mocking or disparaging a rival
religious hymns of praise to God
questions.explanation: Hija' is the genre of satirical, often biting poetry used to mock or attack a rival, prominently exemplified by the naqa'id exchanges between Jarir and Al-Farazdaq.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Madih (مدح), another recognised genre of classical Arabic poetry, is primarily concerned with
options: praise, often directed at a ruler, patron, or notable figure
questions.explanation: Madih is the panegyric genre of Arabic poetry, composed to praise a ruler, patron, or other esteemed individual, often in exchange for reward.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The study of Arabic literature across Pre-Islamic, Islamic, Modern, and West African periods primarily serves to help students
options: memorise only grammar rules with no cultural context
avoid any study of poetry altogether
understand the historical breadth and cultural diversity of the Arabic literary tradition
questions.explanation: Surveying Arabic literature across these varied periods and regions gives students a broad appreciation of its long history and the diverse cultural contexts in which it developed.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: What is the Arabic word for 'book' (كتاب) commonly transliterated as?
questions.explanation: Kitab (كتاب) is the Arabic word for 'book', a term also familiar from its wide use across many languages influenced by Arabic.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: In Arabic grammar, what is the term for a verbal sentence that begins with a verb (فعل)?
questions.explanation: A jumla fi'liyyah is a verbal sentence, one that begins with a verb, as opposed to a jumla ismiyyah which begins with a noun.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: What does 'salam' (سلام) mean in Arabic?
questions.explanation: Salam (سلام) means 'peace' and forms the root of the common Arabic greeting 'as-salamu alaykum'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which case ending (i'rab) typically marks the subject (fa'il) of a verbal sentence in Classical Arabic?
questions.explanation: The subject (fa'il) of a verbal sentence in Classical Arabic is typically marked with the nominative case ending, marfu'.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: What is the Arabic term for a 'root letter' system (usually three consonants) that underlies most word derivations?
questions.explanation: Jadhr refers to the root — typically a set of three consonants — from which most Arabic words are derived through various patterns.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: The Arabic numeral system, widely used worldwide today, is often referred to in English by what name reflecting its transmission route?
questions.explanation: The base-10 positional numeral system now used worldwide is called 'Arabic numerals' in English, reflecting its transmission to Europe via the Arab world (though it originated in India).

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: What does 'kitabah' (كتابة) refer to as a skill area in Arabic language learning?
questions.explanation: Kitabah refers to writing, one of the four core language skills (alongside listening, speaking, and reading) emphasised in Arabic language study.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: Which of these best describes 'tajweed' in the context of Qur'anic study?
options: The set of rules governing the correct pronunciation and recitation of the Qur'an
questions.explanation: Tajweed refers to the rules governing correct pronunciation and articulation during Qur'anic recitation.

questions.subject: Arabic
questions.text: What is the Arabic word for 'teacher' (معلم) commonly transliterated as?
questions.explanation: Mu'allim (معلم) is the Arabic word for 'teacher' or 'instructor'.
